row.evidence: Sinch's Build Dashboard docs cover inviting teammates by email and SAML 2.0 SSO enabled on request; no SCIM endpoint is documented and the help centre returns no SCIM articles.
row.notes: CPaaS with usage-based pricing (no seat tiers). SAML SSO for the Sinch Build Dashboard (Sinch ID) is a request-only pilot verified with Entra ID and Okta; Okta's OIN app is SAML-only. Users are invited by email in Settings > Users with one of five roles. No SCIM found in the developer docs sitemap, llms.txt or help-centre search, so status is none by absence. Sub-brands (Mailgun, Mailjet, Sinch Engage, Contact Pro) were not researched separately.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go
plans.price_text: Usage-based (per message / per minute), no per-seat plans
plans.notes: Sinch publishes per-channel usage pricing, not seat tiers. SAML SSO is enabled on request through support (pilot), not tied to a named plan.

okta.notes: OIN page has only SAML checked; SCIM and provisioning capabilities unchecked.

entra.notes: No Learn tutorial found at saas-apps/sinch-tutorial (404). Sinch says its SAML is verified with Entra ID as a custom SAML app.

citations.title: Pricing | Sinch
citations.quote: Our pay-as-you-go pricing for SMS offers the transparency, flexibility, and competitiveness you need to take your communications to the next level.

citations.title: Team & access management | Sinch
citations.quote: Sinch accounts and projects can be shared with teammates. This page covers inviting them, controlling what they can do with roles, and managing settings that apply to your whole organization.

citations.title: Team & access management | Sinch
citations.quote: Remove a member to revoke their access immediately. Any [access keys](/docs/identity-access-management/access/access-keys) they created keep working until deleted, because keys belong to the project, not the person.

citations.title: Team & access management | Sinch
citations.quote: Enter each person's email address and choose a role (see below).

citations.title: Sinch ID & Single Sign-On | Sinch
citations.quote: Single Sign-On lets your team sign in to Sinch with your company's existing identity provider (IdP) over SAML 2.0. Access is governed by your IdP, so removing a user there removes their Sinch access too.

citations.title: Sinch ID & Single Sign-On | Sinch
citations.quote: SSO is a request-only feature: you ask Sinch to enable it for your account rather than switching it on yourself.

citations.title: Sinch ID & Single Sign-On | Sinch
citations.quote: Sinch ID SSO uses SAML 2.0 and is verified with Microsoft Entra ID and Okta. Other SAML 2.0 identity providers generally connect the same way.

citations.title: How do I get access to SAML ? | Sinch Support
citations.quote: To access Sinch ID SAML during this pilot phase, please reach out to Sinch support clearly explaining your requirements.

citations.title: Sinch | Okta Integration Network
citations.quote: SAML Single Sign-On for secure access to the Sinch dashboard, ensuring centralized identity management for teams managing communication APIs.

open_questions: No SCIM endpoint or user-management API (beyond the access-keys API for application credentials) is documented for the Sinch Build Dashboard.
Docs do not say whether SAML SSO auto-creates (JIT) users or whether users must first be invited.
Whether SSO (pilot, request-only) carries a contract or price requirement is not published.
Sub-brands (Mailgun, Mailjet, Sinch Engage, Contact Pro, MessageMedia) have separate admin consoles and were not researched individually.
